title: John Davenant: Dissertationes duae (De morte Christi Cap. 1-4 partial) (New English tip)

records.label: Section 1 — Christ's death was meant for peace, yet curiosity turns it into dispute; both sides already grant a twofold consideration
Section 2 — Thesis 1: Christ's death is proposed in Scripture as a universal remedy applicable to every person unto salvation
Section 3 — Thesis 1 continued: John 3:16 does not restrict the death to the elect; Testimonies 2–3
Section 4 — Testimonies 4–5 and the conglobated “for all” texts close Cap. 1’s scriptural proof
Section 5 — Cap. 2 Ratio 1: Christ’s death yields some spiritual fruits even to the non-elect
Section 6 — Cap. 2 Ratios 2–3: He bore the penalty of the whole race; any wayfarer may be called to believe
Section 7 — Cap. 2 Ratio 4: All who hear the Gospel owe gratitude to Christ as Redeemer
Section 8 — Cap. 2 Ratio 5: The title Redeemer and Savior of the world requires a universal applicable cause
Section 9 — Cap. 2 Ratios 6–7: God’s counsel provided a lytron even for those who remain unbelieving; death is ordained before faith
Section 10 — Cap. 2 ultima ratio: As under the covenant of nature, so under grace salvation is obtainable for all — Cap. 2 closes
Section 11 — Cap. 3 Satisfit: preface — we do not defend a de-facto salvation already obtained for every person
Section 12 — Cap. 3 Obj. 1: Many were already damned when Christ died — how then was his death ever applicable to them?
Section 13 — Cap. 3 Obj. 2: Why ordain a precious remedy as applicable to reprobates God foresaw would never use it?
Section 14 — Cap. 3 Obj. 3: If applicable to all, why was Christ's death never announced to whole nations?
Section 15 — Cap. 3 Obj. 4: If the death is applicable to all, are resurrection, intercession, and mediation likewise?
Section 16 — Cap. 3 Obj. 5: Universal satisfaction would punish the same sins twice — so how can justice stand?
Section 17 — Cap. 3 Obj. 6: Is there any middle between bare sufficiency of the price and real application?
Section 18 — Cap. 3 Obj. 7: Father and Spirit save only the elect — must the Son's oblation be equally narrow?
Section 19 — Cap. 3 Obj. 8: Applicable-to-all death would erase elect/non-elect and overturn predestination
Section 20 — Cap. 3 Obj. 9: A-pari — dying for the unsaved as absurd as saving those Christ did not die for
Section 21 — Cap. 3 Obj. 10: Scriptures restrict the giving of the Son to believers alone
Section 22 — Cap. 3 Obj. 11: Death not applicable to those for whom Christ was not offered — the non-elect
Section 23 — Cap. 3 Obj. 12: Redeemer ordained from special good-pleasure only, not common love of the race
Section 24 — Cap. 3 Obj. 13: If applicable to all, divine wisdom and power would save all
Section 25 — Cap. 3 Obj. 14: If Christ died for all, did he love all with supreme and equal love?
Section 26 — Cap. 3 Obj. 15: Wisely destined means do not exceed their adequate end — the elect’s salvation
Section 27 — Cap. 3 Obj. 16: Application already firm in the death itself — so not applicable where not applied
Section 28 — Cap. 3 Obj. 17 (ultima) and Cap. 3 close: Places naming the elect do not cancel the race-wide covenant
Section 29 — Cap. 4 Tip: Thesis 2 — Christ died sufficiently for all by ordained sufficiency, not bare price-value
Section 30 — Cap. 4 Terms 2–3: Evangelical covenant from the blood; possible faith; three members announced
Section 31 — Cap. 4 Mem. 1 Rat. 1–2: Bare intrinsic sufficiency cannot ground ‘died sufficiently for all’
Section 32 — Cap. 4 Mem. 1 Rat. 3: Sufficient for humans as denied for fallen angels — objection and reply
Section 33 — Cap. 4 Mem. 1 Rat. 4 and close: Piscator/Pareus; intent vs ordination; first member closed
